provenance.note: The unit here is a type system, so the evidence has two halves. The run-time half is **executed**: every guard and every assertion is called on its own route, on another, on a message whose declared payload is absent, and on six shapes that are not messages, with the exact verdict or error recorded. The compile-time half is **read from the syntax tree**, because there is nothing to execute. No key is derived and no client is built; nothing here is secret.

revocation_hides_its_anchor.generated_schema: MultisigRevokeEmbeds: { rev: components['schemas']['REV_V_1']; anc: | components['schemas']['IXN_V_1'] | components['schemas']['IXN_V_2'] | components['schemas']['ICP_V_1'] | components['schemas']['ICP_V_2'] | components['schemas']['ROT_V_1'] | components['schemas']['ROT_V_2'] | components['schemas']['DIP_V_1'] | components['schemas']['DIP_V_2'] | components['schemas']['DRT_V_1'] | components['schemas']['DRT_V_2']; };
revocation_hides_its_anchor.note: `MultisigRevExchange` declares `e: { rev, d? }` where the generated schema's `MultisigRevokeEmbeds` declares `{ rev, anc }`. The hand-written variant hides the anchoring key event, so a caller who narrows through `assertMultisigRev` cannot reach it — while `assertMultisigVcp` and `assertMultisigIss`, whose schema counterparts carry the same field, both expose it.
revocation_hides_its_anchor.rust_decision: `ExchangeEmbed` models the schema, so `ExchangeEmbed::Revocation` carries the anchor and this port keeps it. The schema is generated from a live KERIA and the hand-written variant is the outlier; nothing is hidden.

a_grant_and_an_issuance_share_one_embed.note: `IpexGrantExchange.e` and `MultisigIssExchange.e` declare the same three fields, so one embed shape serves two routes on opposite sides of the table
a_grant_and_an_issuance_share_one_embed.rust_decision: reused rather than duplicated: `MultisigIssuanceEmbed` decodes both, which is why eight schema embed shapes cover nine of the thirteen routes.

the_schema_models_no_ipex_embed.note: the schema's `ExnEmbeds` union has exactly eight members, all multisig; an IPEX offer's `e: { acdc }` is not among them, and apply, agree, and admit declare `e: object`
the_schema_models_no_ipex_embed.rust_decision: the IPEX payloads are modelled here rather than added to `ExchangeEmbed`, because they were never part of the schema's union and widening a verified untagged enum would change how existing documents decode.

the_schema_names_no_group_attribute.note: `gid`, `smids`, and `rmids` appear zero times in the generated schema. The `a` block shapes exist only in this file's hand-written types, which is why they are checked against what the integration tests actually send rather than against a schema.
the_schema_names_no_group_attribute.rust_decision: one `GroupAttributes` value, with the route deciding which of its optional fields are required.

a_guard_narrows_without_checking.guard: export function isMultisigIcp(msg: ExnMessage): msg is ExnMessage { return msg.exn.r === MULTISIG_ICP_ROUTE; }
a_guard_narrows_without_checking.variant: export type MultisigIcpExchange = ExchangeResourceV1 & { exn: ExnV1 & { r: typeof MULTISIG_ICP_ROUTE; e: { icp: Icp | Dip; d?: string; }; a: { gid: string; smids: string[]; rmids?: string[]; [key: string]: unknown; }; }; };
a_guard_narrows_without_checking.note: every guard and every assertion is one route comparison. The variant it narrows to declares an `e` block and an `a` block, and neither is looked at — so `assertMultisigIcp` accepts a message on `/multisig/icp` carrying no `icp` at all, hands back a value typed as though it did, and the caller's `exn.e.icp` is `undefined` while the compiler says it is an inception.
a_guard_narrows_without_checking.rust_decision: the classifier decodes the payload the route promises, so a route and a payload that disagree are a typed refusal rather than a wrong type. That is the whole difference between the two: upstream the narrowing is a claim, here it is a check.

the_guards_have_no_consumers.note: thirteen exported type guards, zero call sites anywhere in the pinned tree outside their own declaration — and six of the thirteen assertions beside them have none either. Nineteen of the twenty-six are dead exports; the seven that are used account for nineteen call sites, all in `test-integration/multisig*.test.ts`.
the_guards_have_no_consumers.rust_decision: not ported as functions. A guard is `matches!` on the classified enum, which costs nothing and cannot drift from the assertion beside it — the same reasoning that recorded `Unqualified` and `CredentialTypes` as having no Rust equivalent, applied to a capability the enum simply subsumes.

a_guard_and_its_assertion_disagree_on_a_.declaration: function assertRoute<T extends ExnMessage>( msg: T, route: string, label: string ): T { if (msg.exn?.r !== route) { throw new Error(`Expected ${label} but got route: ${msg.exn?.r}`); } return msg; }
a_guard_and_its_assertion_disagree_on_a_.note: `assertRoute` reads `msg.exn?.r` and every guard reads `msg.exn.r`, so a value with no `exn` gives the assertion a clean `Error` and the guard a `TypeError`. Two functions that differ by one question mark and by which exception a caller has to catch.
a_guard_and_its_assertion_disagree_on_a_.rust_decision: unrepresentable: a classified message is decoded from a typed `ExchangeResource`, which has no shape without an `exn`.

the_failure_message_repeats_the_route.note: `Expected ${label} but got route: ${msg.exn?.r}` interpolates a value that came from the agent into the error a caller logs
the_failure_message_repeats_the_route.rust_decision: the refusal names the route it expected and the route it found, both bounded — the found one is the message's own field, already length-bounded by the transport's response limit, and neither is formatted into a message a caller is invited to trust.

the_route_table_is_not_closed.note: thirteen constants, and the reference's own `Challenges.respond` sends a fourteenth — `/challenge/response` — which no variant, guard, or assertion names. Every guard simply returns false for it and every assertion throws.
the_route_table_is_not_closed.rust_decision: the classifier has an `Other` case rather than refusing: a route this table does not name is a message, not an error, because this crate itself sends one. Only a *named* route whose payload disagrees is refused.

only_multisig_routes_have_a_group_varian.note: the eight multisig routes each have a `*Group` variant for the form a group request returns; the five IPEX routes have none, so `assertIpexGrant(msg: ExnMultisig)` returns the unnarrowed `ExnMultisig`
only_multisig_routes_have_a_group_varian.rust_decision: one classifier over both containers. The group form differs only in its wrapper — `paths` beside `pathed`, plus three optional labels — so the message inside it classifies identically and the asymmetry disappears.
